text:
maya: Heads-up — noticed SAST nightly run failed for multiple repos after RBAC tweak to keystore roles. Error: KMS decrypt denied. Anyone oncall?
josh: saw that, digging. which job id?
maya: job id `sast-nightly/2026-03-19-03` — logs show `403 AccessDenied: decrypt` from keystore service.
anita: that was from last week's keystore role pruning (PR #1214). I reverted a subset but maybe not all service accounts.
devsec-bot: Alert: 3 repositories failed scans (redwood-core, inference-runtime, infra-config). Failure signature: KMS_DECRYPT_FAIL_V1.
dave: quick triage: is this blocking release? probably not; but blocks evidence update and triage workflows for new findings.
erin: repro command I ran: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://keystore.internal/v1/decrypt | jq .error` -> `{"code":"AccessDenied","message":"principal not authorized to decrypt"}`
josh: can someone paste IAM policy snippet for the ephemeral scanner principal?
maya: pasted policy below
```
serviceAccount:ci-scanner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com
roles:
 - roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
 - roles/logging.logWriter
```
anita: oh we removed `cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` from the key-level binding and only left project role. Keys are key-specific; need grant on key resource.
dave: fix options:
- re-grant key binding to ci-scanner (fastest)
- run scans with fallback scanning agent using local offline scanner (temp)
- revert RBAC prune (risky)
erin: prefer re-grant. who's owner of keystore key? @carla?
carla: I can re-add key binding, will do a short maintenance window ~5m. patch and note in audit log.
josh: also note for SDLC: we should add scan service principal as keystore exception in CHANGELOG and add test in CI.
anita: agree, also add automated check that SAST agents can decrypt sample blob during preflight.
devsec-bot: Audit Event: role.bind key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/sdlc/cryptoKeys/scan-key bound to serviceAccount:ci-scanner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com by carla@redwood.com timestamp 4812345708
maya: after carla's change, reran `sast-nightly/2026-03-19-03` -> `Exit 0, 0 new high findings`. Looks green.
dave: about the high finding in inference-runtime: `CVE-2024-XXXX` marked high for path traversal — is it real?
erin: I reviewed stacktrace — it's a SAST pattern on `utils/path_join` that uses `os.path.join` incorrectly but it's sanitized elsewhere at runtime. Marking as FP but add runtime check.
josh: propose label workflow: `security:needs-evidence` -> `security:fp-acknowledged` if triage shows FP. Add automated comment template on PR.
anita: I can add a pre-commit hook to suppress that rule for flagged functions with comment `# security-ignore: PATH_JOIN_SANITIZE` and require justification.
maya: ok let's track follow-ups: (1) carla rebind key (done) (2) josh add CI decrypt preflight (3) anita add suppression workflow & template (4) dave open vulnerability evidence ticket: #2248
dave: opened ticket #2248 with links to logs and proof-of-fix.
maya: thanks all :thumbsup: closing thread.
